hero.title: Hear every voice in your language.
hero.lead: Live AI dubbing and bilingual subtitles for any video — in your browser, on your desktop or from a file. Understand courses, films, podcasts and streams in the language you think in.

features.title: Everything you need to understand any video
features.lead: Dub it, caption it, mix it, export it — every piece works on its own.

dubbing.title: Live dubbing
dubbing.text: Hear any video spoken in your language while it plays. Natural AI voices keep up with the speaker.

captions.title: Dual subtitles
captions.text: Original and translated captions side by side, on a frosted-glass card you can drag, resize and fade.

outputs.title: Four independent outputs
outputs.text: Original audio, dubbed audio, source subtitles, translated subtitles — switch each one on or off.

mixer.title: A mixer you control
mixer.text: Balance the original against the dub, with smart ducking that lowers the original while the dub speaks.

sync.title: Synchronized player
sync.text: Capture runs ahead while an independent player pauses, seeks and goes fullscreen. Export WebM and SRT.

desktop.title: Desktop app & files
desktop.text: Translate any program’s audio live, or drop in an audio or video file and get a synced player, subtitles and a ZIP.

languages.title: 79 languages
languages.text: Choose your target language from the full Gemini set — the most popular ones come first.

private.title: Private by design
private.text: No analytics, no ads, no relay servers. Audio goes straight to the AI provider you choose.

open.title: Free & open source
open.text: MIT-licensed. Bring your own free API keys, read every line, make it yours.

guide.title: Up and running in minutes
guide.lead: Follow along here, or watch the tutorial video above.

extension.title: Install the extension
extension.text: Add Avorythm from the Chrome Web Store and pin it to your toolbar. In Edge, use the same listing — or load the ZIP from the release page.

extension.title: Add your free Gemini key
extension.text: Create a key in Google AI Studio, then open Avorythm → Settings → “Connect to Gemini”, paste it and press Save. Finally tick the consent box so audio can be sent to Google Gemini — nothing is captured before you press Start.

extension.title: Choose language and mode
extension.text: Open the popup and pick a target language, then “On this page” (lowest delay) or “Synchronized recorder & player” (steady sync, seeking and export).

extension.title: Press Start on any video
extension.text: Open a normal video tab and press Start translating. Hear the dub, read both captions and drag the glass card wherever you like.

extension.title: Make it yours
extension.text: Switch the four outputs on or off, balance the original against the dub, and set the subtitle size and opacity in Settings.

desktop.title: Download the installer
desktop.text: Get the build for your system from Releases. The Windows installer already includes FFmpeg.

desktop.title: Add your keys
desktop.text: Open Advanced settings and save a Gemini key (plus a Groq key for file processing). Keys live in your operating system’s keyring.

desktop.title: Route the audio
desktop.text: To translate another program live, send its sound to a loopback device — AMM Virtual Audio on Windows, BlackHole on macOS, a monitor source on Linux — and pick it as the app’s audio input.

desktop.title: Press Start translation
desktop.text: Choose your language and output mix, then press Start translation. Keep the listening output on your real headphones.

files.title: Open File Studio
files.text: In the desktop app, open File Studio and drop in an audio or video file (up to 8 GB).

files.title: Pick language, voice and mode
files.text: Choose the target language and a voice. “Precise” gives tighter sync; “Fast” finishes sooner.

files.title: Start processing
files.text: Leave Avorythm running while it transcribes, translates, narrates and aligns your file.

files.title: Play or download
files.text: Watch in the synchronized player, or download original.wav, dubbed.wav, source.srt and translated.srt — or everything as one ZIP.

languages.title: 79 languages, one click
languages.lead: Pick your target language from the full Gemini set — popular ones first, from Arabic and Chinese to Swahili and Zulu.
languages.ui: The interface is available in English, Persian and Simplified Chinese; dubbing and captions work in all 79 languages.

privacy.title: Private by design
privacy.lead: Avorythm is built so that nobody — including us — sits between you and your media.

items.title: No analytics, ads or telemetry
items.text: There is no tracking code in the app, the extension or this website.

items.title: Your keys, your device
items.text: API keys stay in your browser session by default, or in your operating system’s keyring on desktop.

items.title: Straight to the AI provider
items.text: Audio goes directly from your device to Google Gemini — and, in precise mode, short windows to Groq Whisper. Never to a server of ours.

items.title: Consent first
items.text: Capture starts only after you give consent and press Start, and you can stop at any moment.

items.title: Open source (MIT)
items.text: Every line is public. Read it, audit it, improve it.

privacy.note: Avorythm relies on preview AI services. Accuracy, voices, latency and quotas can change — double-check anything important.

download.unsigned: The Windows installer is unsigned while code-signing approval is pending, so Windows may warn about an unrecognized publisher. Verify your download against SHA256SUMS.txt from the same release.

items.a: Yes. The extension and the desktop app are free and open source (MIT). They use your own API keys: Google AI Studio offers a free Gemini tier, and Groq’s free tier powers Whisper for files. Provider limits and quotas apply and can change.

items.q: Do I need the desktop app to use the extension?
items.a: No. The extension is fully standalone — no desktop app, Python, FFmpeg, localhost or virtual audio cable. The desktop app is for translating other programs’ audio and for processing files.

items.q: Which sites does it work on?
items.a: Any normal web page that plays audio or video in Chrome or Edge 116+. DRM-protected streams and browser-internal pages (such as chrome://) can block capture; use the “On this page” mode when video capture isn’t possible.

Live translation has to hear a phrase before it can speak it, so a small delay is unavoidable. “On this page” is the lowest-delay path. The synchronized player records ahead (20 seconds by default) so audio, video and captions stay on one timeline.

Capture starts only after you give consent and press Start. Audio goes straight from your browser to Google Gemini — and, in precise mode, short windows to Groq Whisper — never to servers of ours. There are no ads, analytics or telemetry, and keys stay in your browser session unless you choose to remember them.
79 target languages, from English, Persian, Arabic and Chinese to Swahili and Zulu. The interface itself is in English, Persian and Simplified Chinese, with more planned.
Avorythm uses preview AI services. Accuracy, voices, latency and quotas can change, and no AI translation is perfect — double-check anything important.

items.q: Does it work in Firefox or Safari?
items.a: Not yet. Avorythm supports Chrome and Edge (Chromium 116 or newer). Edge users can install it from the Chrome Web Store listing; a dedicated Microsoft Edge Add-ons listing is on the roadmap.

A code-signing application with the SignPath Foundation is pending. Until it’s approved, Windows SmartScreen may show an unrecognized-publisher warning. Verify your download against SHA256SUMS.txt from the same release.
